name: Dashboard & Analytics – Visitor Statistics, AI Traffic & PageSpeed Test by Swift Web Dev
author: Rasel Hakkani

sections.description:
Your whole site at a glance: visitors, speed and health on one modern dashboard

SwiftWebDev Dashboard & Analytics adds a clean, colorful home screen to WordPress that answers the questions you ask every day: how many people visited, which pages they read, where they came from, how fast is the site, and is anything out of date?

No cookies, no Google Analytics account and no API key for speed tests. Install, activate and your dashboard is ready.

The plugin is lightweight by design. The front end gets one small counter script that runs after the page has loaded, and WordPress checks the browser name of each request for known AI bots and search crawlers. Everything else happens in the admin area.

📊 Cookieless visitor stats

  • Real people only: a visit counts once there is a sign of a person, so bots, crawlers and automated page loads never inflate your visitors
  • Visitors, page views and sessions for the last 7, 30 or 90 days
  • Visitors over time chart, busiest days of the week and engagement (pages per visit, visits per visitor, best day)
  • Trend versus the previous period, with a sparkline on every card
  • Top pages, referrers and devices for the selected period
  • A views column on your Posts and Pages lists, plus a compact visitor counter widget on the classic WordPress dashboard
  • Counted on your own site, stored in your own database
  • No cookies or browser storage, and IP addresses are never saved
  • Logged-in users are not counted by default

🤖 AI traffic and AI crawlers

  • AI crawlers: how often AI bots such as GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot, Meta and Amazon visit, by company, with the last day each was seen
  • Each bot visit is sorted by purpose: training, AI search, or asked by a user
  • People from AI assistants in the same card: visitors who clicked a link to your site in ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, Claude, Copilot and 6 more assistants, with the top assistants and the change versus the previous period, so you see how much AI reads and how many people it sends
  • AI assistants are tagged “AI” in your Referrers list
  • Bots & automated visits: automated browser visits, AI crawlers and search & SEO crawlers (such as Googlebot, Bingbot, AhrefsBot, social link previews and uptime monitors), each with its change versus the previous period. None of them count as visitors
  • AI access check: reads your robots.txt and shows, per AI company, whether AI search and training crawlers are allowed or blocked, with a clear warning when AI search is blocked
  • Shows whether your site has an llms.txt file
  • Counted on your own server; nothing is sent to AI companies or anyone else

✉️ Weekly Site Report email

  • One email every Monday: visitors, top pages, top referrers and AI visitors with the change from the week before, bots and automated visits, speed scores, pending updates and Site Health
  • Sent from your own site with WordPress mail, to the address you choose
  • Off by default; turn it on in the plugin settings and send yourself a test first

⚡ PageSpeed scores with fixes

  • Google PageSpeed scores for mobile and desktop, run with one click
  • Test your homepage or any other page of your site
  • Performance, Accessibility, Best practices and SEO scores
  • Core Web Vitals from the lab test, plus real-user Chrome UX data when Google has it
  • A ranked list of what to fix to reach 90+, written in plain language
  • No Google API key needed

🩺 Updates and site health

  • Pending WordPress, plugin and theme updates
  • Your PHP version, with the recommended version
  • Site Health status with a shortcut to run the checks
  • Recent activity: published posts and pages, new users, plugin and theme updates

🔗 Quick links

  • One-click shortcuts to the WordPress tasks you use most
  • Pin, reorder and hide shortcuts, and search them
  • Each user keeps their own pinned list

🎨 A modern admin experience

  • A matching modern style for the WordPress admin menu on every admin page
  • Your own logo and site name at the top of the menu
  • Search from the dashboard header: posts and pages in any status (drafts too), media, users and every admin screen, with icons, recent items and quick actions.
  • Live visitors in the WordPress toolbar while you browse your site: how many people are online now, with today’s visitors, page views, AI visits, top pages and sources on hover, plus the same search from a toolbar icon. Both can be turned off in Settings.
  • Show, hide and drag dashboard cards into your own order
  • Optionally open this dashboard after login, with the classic WordPress dashboard one click away
  • Administrators get the new look; other users keep the normal WordPress admin

🏆 PRO add-on

Everything described above is included in this plugin, with no limits, license keys or time restrictions. For extra reports, SwiftWebDev Dashboard PRO is a separate add-on plugin, sold and downloaded from our website: real-time visitors, countries and browsers, goals and conversions, UTM campaigns, AI assistant landing pages, traffic-spike email alerts, form and click tracking, session recordings, CSV export and weekly scheduled speed tests. Learn more about the PRO add-on

🔒 Privacy

Free visitor stats are counted without cookies or browser storage. Each visit is identified by a one-way hash of the IP address and browser, combined with a random value that changes every day, so visitors cannot be followed from one day to the next. IP addresses and browser details are never saved. To tell people from bots, the counter script only notices that the mouse moved, the page scrolled, a key or the screen was pressed, or the page stayed open for 10 seconds; it records nothing about what was done. Raw visit records are deleted after 48 hours; daily totals of visitors and automated visits are kept for 180 days (the longest period shown, plus the period before it for comparison). Daily counts per page, referring website and device type are kept for 90 days; daily counts per AI assistant are kept for 180 days.

AI crawlers and search, SEO, social and uptime crawlers are recognized by the name in their user agent (for example GPTBot or Googlebot). The plugin stores only a daily total per crawler, kept for 180 days. No IP address, user agent or requested address is stored. All data stays in your WordPress database.

More free plugins by the author

  • SourceSay: ask WooCommerce customers “How did you hear about us?” after checkout and see revenue by channel.

External services

This plugin connects to the Swift Web Dev API for two things, and only when an administrator asks it to.

SwiftWebDev speed test service (swdashapi.swiftoutbox.com), which uses the Google PageSpeed Insights API

Used to measure the speed scores shown on the Speed & Optimize screen and the dashboard. A request is sent only when an administrator clicks “Run test”. The request contains your site address, the address of the page to test (your homepage or another page of your site) and the test type (mobile or desktop). Our service checks that the page belongs to your site, then asks Google PageSpeed Insights to test it with our own Google API key and returns the result. No visitor data is sent. The service keeps the result in memory for up to 10 minutes, so a repeat test of the same page returns quickly, then discards it; test results are never saved to disk or a database. When a test runs, the service saves your site address and the time of the test, so we know which sites use the speed test.

  • Swift Web Dev terms of service: https://swiftwebdev.com/terms/
  • Swift Web Dev privacy policy: https://swiftwebdev.com/privacy-policy/
  • Google PageSpeed Insights: https://developers.google.com/speed/docs/insights/v5/about
  • Google terms of service: https://developers.google.com/terms
  • Google privacy policy: https://policies.google.com/privacy

Optional: tell Swift Web Dev this site uses the plugin (swdashapi.swiftoutbox.com)

Off by default. Nothing is sent unless an administrator turns on “Tell Swift Web Dev this site uses the plugin” in the plugin settings or on the welcome screen. When it is on, the plugin sends your site address and the plugin version once a week, so we know which sites use the plugin. No visitor data, user data, email address or content is sent. Turning the setting off, or deactivating the plugin, asks the service to remove your site from the list.

  • Swift Web Dev terms of service: https://swiftwebdev.com/terms/
  • Swift Web Dev privacy policy: https://swiftwebdev.com/privacy-policy/

Your own robots.txt and llms.txt (not an external service)

The AI access check reads /robots.txt and /llms.txt from your own site address, at most once every 12 hours while an administrator views the dashboard. These requests go to your own site only; nothing is sent to a third party.

Third-party libraries

All are bundled locally (nothing is loaded from a CDN) and GPL-compatible:

  • SortableJS, MIT license (assets/vendor/sortable/LICENSE).
  • Plus Jakarta Sans font, SIL Open Font License 1.1 (assets/fonts/OFL.txt).
  • Simple Icons brand icons (https://simpleicons.org), CC0 1.0 (includes/brands.php).
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate SwiftWebDev Dashboard & Analytics from the Plugins screen.
  2. Open SWD Dashboard in the admin menu.
  3. Optional: in the plugin settings (user menu, top right), set your own sidebar logo and name.
sections.faq:
Does the plugin slow down my site?

The visitor counter is a small script that sends one request when a page has loaded and one more when it sees a person (see the next question). The plugin adds nothing else to your front end.

How do you tell people from bots?

A visit counts once the visitor moves the mouse, scrolls, taps, types or keeps the page open for 10 seconds. Everything else is counted separately as automated: page loads with none of these signs (often headless browsers and scripts), AI crawlers such as GPTBot, and search and SEO crawlers such as Googlebot or AhrefsBot. You see all three on the Bots & automated visits card and in the weekly email. They never count as visitors, page views or sessions.

Why do the speed tests not work on my local site?

Google can only test websites that are reachable on the public internet. Run the test on your live site.

Do I need a Google API key for speed tests?

No. Speed tests run through the SwiftWebDev speed test service with our own key. You can test your homepage or any other page of your site.

Can I still use the normal WordPress dashboard?

Yes. The WordPress Dashboard menu item is not changed. You can also open your user menu in the plugin and choose “Classic WordPress dashboard”. “Open SWD Dashboard after login” is off by default; you can turn it on in the plugin settings.

How do I see traffic from ChatGPT in WordPress?

Open the dashboard and look at People from AI assistants in the AI crawlers card; AI assistants are also tagged “AI” in Referrers. A visit counts when it arrives from an AI assistant such as ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, Claude or Copilot, either through the referring address or the utm_source tag some assistants add to their links (ChatGPT adds utm_source=chatgpt.com). It is counted once per visit, on your own site, without cookies.

Why does some ChatGPT traffic show as direct?

Some apps open links without a referring address or a utm_source tag. Those visits cannot be told apart from people who typed your address, so they count as direct visits.

Does it track Google AI Overviews?

No. Google does not mark clicks from AI Overviews or AI Mode, so they arrive as normal Google search visits and show under Referrers as Google, the same as in Google Analytics.

Which AI bots crawl my site, and what is the difference between GPTBot, OAI-SearchBot and ChatGPT-User?

The AI crawlers card lists every AI company whose bots visited, such as OpenAI, Anthropic, Perplexity, Meta, Amazon and Apple. OpenAI runs three: GPTBot collects pages to train its models (Training), OAI-SearchBot indexes pages for ChatGPT search answers (AI search), and ChatGPT-User opens a page when someone asks ChatGPT to (Asked by a user). Other companies work the same way. Bots are recognized by the name they send, which is not proof of identity.

Why are AI crawler counts lower than my server logs?

Page caching. When a cache plugin or your host answers a request before WordPress runs, the plugin cannot count it. The card then says the counts are a minimum. Your cache settings may let you exclude AI bots (often called “rejected user agents”).

Should I block AI crawlers?

It is your choice. Blocking training crawlers keeps your pages out of AI model training. Blocking AI search crawlers keeps your pages out of AI answers, which also means those assistants cannot link to you. The AI access check shows what your robots.txt allows today; it never changes it.

What is in the weekly email?

Last week’s visitors, page views and sessions compared with the week before, your top pages and referrers, AI traffic, bots and automated visits, the latest speed scores, pending updates and the Site Health status. It is off until you turn it on.
sections.changelog:
1.3.1

  • New: optional “Tell Swift Web Dev this site uses the plugin” setting. Off by default; when on, it sends only your site address and the plugin version once a week.
  • Fixed: after updating to 1.3.0, some icons could be missing (for example in the PRO add-on notice) until the browser cache was cleared.

1.3.0

  • New: “Improvement areas” on the Speed screen now has four tabs, Performance, Accessibility, Best practices and SEO, each with its own list of things to fix, a count and plain-English advice.
  • New: Quick Links is now a full-width row right under the visitor cards, with your shortcuts side by side.
  • New: the menu logo is cropped to a square with the WordPress crop screen when you choose it.
  • New: “Use the site icon as the menu logo” switch in the settings.
  • New: your profile picture in the header. Without a picture, the first letter of your first name is shown on a colored background.
  • Changed: the plugin is now called “SWD Dashboard” inside WordPress, and the listing name ends with “by Swift Web Dev”.
  • Improved: the weekly report email field no longer shows the site admin email as its example.
  • Improved: titles of speed checks that mention HTML tags are now shown in full.
  • Improved: new look for the optional PRO add-on notice.

1.2.0

  • Improved: visitors are now real people only. A visit counts once the visitor moves the mouse, scrolls, taps, types or keeps the page open for 10 seconds; page loads without any of these are counted separately as automated visits.
  • New: Bots & automated visits card with automated browser visits, AI crawlers and search & SEO crawlers, each with the change versus the previous period. None of them count as visitors.
  • New: search, SEO, social and uptime crawlers (such as Googlebot, Bingbot, AhrefsBot, SemrushBot, link previews and UptimeRobot) are counted on your server like AI crawlers, as a daily total per crawler.
  • Changed: AI visitors moved into the AI crawlers card as “People from AI assistants”, with the top AI assistants.
  • New: an “AI” tag marks AI assistants such as ChatGPT and Perplexity in Referrers.
  • New: the weekly email lists bots and automated visits: automated browser visits, AI crawlers and search & SEO crawlers.
  • Changed: the toolbar “online” count and search now show on your site only, not on admin pages, and the online count includes real people only.
  • Fixed: visitors behind Cloudflare or a proxy are counted from their own address, so they are no longer merged into one.
  • Fixed: on sites installed in a subfolder, page paths no longer show the folder name.
  • Improved: easier to read everywhere: darker secondary text, readable toolbar items, KPI numbers no longer cut off on tablets, and the dashboard header works on phones.
  • Improved: the weekly email shows its figures in an even grid and page titles in Top pages.

1.1.0

  • New: top pages, referrers, devices and AI traffic cards on the dashboard.
  • New: AI crawlers card: AI bot visits by company and purpose (training, AI search, asked by a user), counted on your server without storing IP addresses or user agents.
  • New: AI access check: which AI companies your robots.txt allows for AI search and for training, a warning when AI search is blocked, and whether llms.txt exists.
  • New: AI visitors card with the share of all visits and the change versus the previous period.
  • New: AI visitors and AI bot visits in the weekly email.
  • New: Weekly Site Report email (opt-in) with a test send.
  • New: views column on Posts and Pages, and a visitor counter widget on the classic WordPress dashboard.
  • New: one-time welcome screen after install to make SwiftWebDev Dashboard your home screen, and a Settings link on the Plugins screen.
  • New: toolbar items for administrators: visitors online now with a mini dashboard on hover, and a search icon that opens the dashboard search from any admin page.
  • Improved: header search finds posts and pages in any status, media and users, with icons, recent items saved to your account and quick actions.
  • Improved: sticky header on phones and long site names in the sidebar.
  • Readme: disclose that speed test results are kept in memory for up to 10 minutes.

1.0.0

  • First public release: admin dashboard, cookieless visitor stats, Google PageSpeed scores with Core Web Vitals, quick links, updates and site health, modern admin menu.
